claims.statement: The repository ships three compose files for distinct jobs: docker-compose.yml builds the full stack from source, docker-compose.prod.yml pulls GHCR images for pull-based production hosting (host needs only Docker), and docker-compose.dev.yml provides the shared hot-reload development environment driven by ./scripts/dev.sh.

In every composition Postgres runs as postgres:16-alpine with a pg_isready healthcheck, and the api service declares depends_on postgres with condition: service_healthy, so migrations and the Express server never start against a database that cannot accept connections.

Object storage is SeaweedFS running 'server -dir=/data -s3 -s3.port=9000' in the s3_data volume, a drop-in replacement after MinIO removed its public images; the production composition pins chrislusf/seaweedfs:3.80 and publishes no S3 ports, while the source-build and dev compositions track :latest and expose 9000 (S3) and 9333 (master UI).

The Wahapedia sync-worker sits behind profiles: ['tools'] with depends_on postgres: service_healthy in both the source-build and production compositions, so 'docker compose up' never starts it; operators run one-shot ETL passes with 'docker compose run --rm sync-worker' or schedule them on the host, and the image is published to GHCR so no checkout or build is needed.

apps/api/entrypoint.sh is the API container's ENTRYPOINT: with set -e it defaults DIRECT_URL to DATABASE_URL, runs 'npx prisma migrate deploy --schema=packages/db-client/prisma/schema.prisma', then 'exec node apps/api/dist/index.js' — applying pending migrations before the server listens. Because docker-compose.prod.yml sets no DIRECT_URL for api, this default is what makes prod Prisma schema validation work (both compositions do set DIRECT_URL explicitly for sync-worker).
When DATABASE_URL is unset the API entrypoint skips migrations entirely, logs 'catalog-only mode', and still execs the server, so the image boots without a database.

Dockerfile.api's runner stage copies the Prisma schema plus migrations and the Prisma CLI into the image and installs libvips42 for Sharp, making the published image self-contained: 'docker run' against a fresh database self-migrates at boot with no host tooling or compose command override.

Dockerfile.web is a multi-stage Next.js build that bakes a build-time fallback NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:4000/api for SSG prerendering and runs as the non-root nextjs user (uid 1001) exposing port 3000.

Dockerfile.dev bakes only the toolchain (Node 20, npm ci from the lockfile, generated Prisma client, Chromium libraries for Playwright) and a node_modules/.deps-stamp lockfile checksum; source is bind-mounted by docker-compose.dev.yml with container-owned dev_node_modules/dev_web_next/dev_turbo_cache volumes so host edits hot-reload without shadowing dependencies.

Post-deploy verification per docs/DEPLOYMENT.md §3.2 is web login gate on :3000, GET /api/health on :4000 returning success:true, 13 tables in Postgres on :5432 after auto-migration, and HTTP 200 from SeaweedFS on :9000/:9333; the production composition parameterizes API/web ports as ${API_PORT:-4000}/${WEB_PORT:-3000} and publishes no Postgres or S3 ports.

A freshly migrated database is empty; 'npx tsx packages/db-client/prisma/seed.ts' populates core stratagems, datasheets, weapons, and paint swatches and is idempotent because each row is looked up and skipped when it already exists.

The dev composition automates migration and seeding via a one-shot db-init service that probes Postgres with scripts/dev-wait-for-postgres.js, runs migrate deploy plus the seed, then idles with 'tail -f /dev/null' so its logs remain available.

Pull-based production hosting consumes ghcr.io/fatpat81/beerhammer/forceorg-{api,web,sync-worker}:${FORCEORG_TAG:-latest}; the deploy workflow publishes all three images on every push to main tagged latest and github.sha, so update is re-pull + up -d and rollback is re-running with FORCEORG_TAG set to a previous sha.

docker-compose.prod.yml writes every security-relevant variable as ${VAR:-placeholder} (JWT_SECRET=please-change-me, POSTGRES_USER/PASSWORD=postgres/postgrespassword, S3_BUCKET_NAME=forceorg-miniatures, AWS keys and PUBLIC_CDN_BASE_URL default empty) and uses no ${VAR:?} required expansion, so the stack boots with zero configuration by design; docs/DEPLOYMENT.md §2/§3.1 document these as public test-only placeholders that MUST be overridden beyond localhost, and the API auth middleware's own 'dev-secret-change-in-production' fallback means an unoverridden server accepts tokens anyone can mint.

docs/DEPLOYMENT.md hardening guidance: override JWT_SECRET and database/storage credentials, serve the API through a TLS reverse proxy, restrict CORS_ORIGIN to real browser origins, keep Postgres and S3 ports off the public network, and back up the two named volumes (pg_dump plus a copy of s3_data); 'docker compose down' keeps postgres_data while 'down -v' wipes it.

./scripts/dev.sh wraps docker-compose.dev.yml as the single dev entry point (up, down, rebuild, verify, test, e2e/e2e-install, logs, shell, psql), and WEB_PORT/API_PORT environment overrides remap the published host ports on collision.

Table count on a fresh self-migrated database is 13: the init migration 20261005170232_init issues 13 CREATE TABLE statements and schema.prisma declares 13 models, so docs/DEPLOYMENT.md §3.1's '14 tables' statement contradicts both §3.2's verification table (13) and the migration itself.

docker-compose.yml (the from-source composition) hard-codes dev credentials — postgres/postgrespassword, minioadmin/minioadminpassword S3 keys, CORS_ORIGIN, PUBLIC_CDN_BASE_URL — and sets no JWT_SECRET for api at all, so that stack silently authenticates writes with the middleware's dev-secret fallback and is unsafe beyond localhost.

A zero-configuration production boot is only partially functional: health and the login gate work, but with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY defaulting to empty the API has no usable S3 credentials, and with PUBLIC_CDN_BASE_URL empty the storage service derives image URLs from AWS_ENDPOINT (http://s3:9000/<bucket>/<key>), which resolve only inside the compose network.
